s:
With reference to the UPSC, consider the following statements:
1. The UPSC headquarters is at Metcalfe House, Delhi.
2. The first Public Service Commission was set up at Metcalfe House, Delhi.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Only 2 is correct: the first Public Service Commission was set up at Metcalfe House, Delhi. The UPSC headquarters is at Dholpur House, New Delhi.

s: In which year did Satyendranath Tagore clear the ICS?
x: Satyendranath Tagore cleared the ICS in 1863; the examination began in London in 1855 and was first held in India in 1922.

s: On which date was India's first Public Service Commission, whose centenary the UPSC marked in 2026, constituted?
x: India's first PSC was constituted on 1 October 1926; UPSC completed 100 years on 1 October 2026.

s: Who became the first Indian Chairman of the Public Service Commission in 1947?
x: H.K. Kripalani became the first Indian Chairman in 1947; 1937 is when the Federal PSC name came into use.

s: Under Article 323, to whom is the annual report of the UPSC submitted?
x: Article 323 requires the UPSC's annual report to be submitted to the President and laid before Parliament.

s: Which Article provides that the President regulates the conditions of service of PSC members?
x: Article 318 empowers the President to regulate conditions of service; Articles 316 and 317 deal with appointment and removal.

s: Which Article permits Parliament or a State Legislature to extend the functions of Public Service Commissions?
x: Article 321 allows extension of functions; Article 319 bars further employment and Article 320 lists the main functions.

s: Who was the first Chairman of India's Public Service Commission set up in 1926?
x: Sir Ross Barker was the first Chairman in 1926; Kripalani was the first Indian Chairman (1947) and R.N. Banerjee the first UPSC Chairman (1950).

s: In the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2025, women made up 299 of 958 selected candidates. What was their approximate share?
x: Women were 31.2% (299 of 958) in CSE 2025, up from 3.6% in 1952.

s: Which Commission recommended a statutory Public Service Commission in India in 1924?
x: The Lee Commission, chaired by Lord Lee of Fareham, reported in 1924 and recommended a statutory PSC, set up in 1926.

s: Who was the first Chairman of the UPSC after it came into being under the Constitution on 26 January 1950?
x: R.N. Banerjee was the first Chairman of the UPSC under the Constitution; Sir Ross Barker headed the 1926 PSC and H.K. Kripalani was the first Indian Chairman (1947).

s: Under Article 317, removal of a UPSC member on the ground of misbehaviour requires an inquiry by which body?
x: Article 317 lets the President remove a PSC member for misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.

s: Where was the ICS examination held in India for the first time in 1922?
x: The ICS examination was first held in India at Allahabad in 1922 and moved to Delhi in 1928.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Joint Public Service Commission for two or more States?
x: Article 315 provides PSCs for the Union and the States, and a Joint PSC for two or more States.

s: Under which Article is the Chairman of the UPSC made ineligible for further employment under the Government?
x: Article 319 bars the UPSC Chairman from further employment under the Government of India or a State.

s: Where is the headquarters of the UPSC located?
x: The first PSC was set up at Metcalfe House, Delhi; the UPSC headquarters is now at Dholpur House, New Delhi.

s: Who was the chairman of the Lee Commission (1923-24), which recommended a statutory Public Service Commission?
x: The Lee Commission was appointed in 1923 under Lord Lee of Fareham (Arthur Hamilton Lee) and reported in 1924.

s: In 2022, four Group A railway services were unified into which service?
x: In 2022 four Group A railway services were unified as the Indian Railway Management Service.

s: In which year was India's Public Service Commission renamed the Federal Public Service Commission?
x: Under the Government of India Act, 1935 the PSC became the Federal Public Service Commission in 1937.

s: Under the constitutional framework applicable to State ministries, what limit was introduced by the 91st Amendment, 2003?
o: Ministers may not exceed 10% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 15
Ministers may not exceed 15% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 12
Ministers may not exceed 15% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 10
Ministers may not exceed 20% of the Assembly strength, with a minimum of 12
x: The 91st Amendment, 2003 limits a State ministry to 15% of the Assembly strength and prescribes a minimum of 12 ministers. The other options alter either the percentage or the minimum.

s: In October 2026, Om Prakash Mathur was appointed Governor of which State?
x: Om Prakash Mathur was appointed Governor of Kerala; Arlekar went to Tamil Nadu and Dushyant Gautam to Sikkim.

s: Which Article deals with the pardoning power of the Governor?
x: Article 161 deals with the Governor's pardoning power; Articles 156, 157 and 159 cover term, qualifications and oath.

s: Under Article 155, who appoints the Governor of a State?
x: Article 155 provides for the appointment of the Governor by the President, not Parliament.

s: Who was appointed Governor of Tamil Nadu on 12 October 2026?
x: R.V. Arlekar became TN Governor; Om Prakash Mathur moved to Kerala and Dushyant Gautam to Sikkim.

s: Under Article 164(4), for how long at most can a person who is not a member of the Legislature remain a State minister?
x: Article 164(4) allows a non-member to be a minister for six months.

s: Under Article 159, before whom does the Governor of a State take the oath of office?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Article 159: the Governor takes the oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State.

s: Which Telangana Minister, holding Environment, Forests and Endowments, was removed by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on 3 September 2026?
x: CM A. Revanth Reddy removed Minister Konda Surekha, who held Environment, Forests and Endowments, on 3 September 2026.

s: Which Article lays down the duty of the Chief Minister to furnish information to the Governor?
x: Article 167 sets out the Chief Minister's duty to inform the Governor about decisions of the Council of Ministers.

s: Under the State-level Uniform Civil Code measures discussed in September 2026, which population is exempt?
x: State-level Uniform Civil Code measures exempt tribal populations. The other options do not reflect the specified exemption.

s: When will the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill–2026 come into force?
o: After approval by the Supreme Court
x: The Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill–2026 will come into force after the rules are notified. Presidential assent alone does not make the Bill operational under the stated provision.

s: Which case upheld the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986?
x: Daniel Latifi upheld the 1986 Act; Shah Bano concerned maintenance under Section 125 CrPC.

s: Article 44, which deals with the Uniform Civil Code, is placed in which Part of the Constitution?
x: Article 44 is a Directive Principle in Part IV. The Gujarat UCC Bill-2026 also covers live-in relationships.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 44, a Directive Principle in Part IV, directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code.
2. Article 25 deals with freedom of religion.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Article 44 in Part IV concerns the Uniform Civil Code and Article 25 concerns religion.

s: Which of the following pairs (case – legal point) is correctly matched?
o: Shayara Bano – Goa as an example of a common civil code
Jose Paulo Coutinho – Instant triple talaq invalid
Section 6A Citizenship Act case, 2024 – Casteism and gender discrimination cannot claim Article 29 protection
Shayara Bano – Casteism and gender discrimination cannot claim Article 29 protection
x: The Section 6A case (2024) held that casteism and gender discrimination cannot claim Article 29 protection. Shayara Bano invalidated instant triple talaq and Jose Paulo Coutinho cited Goa's common civil code.

s: Which case held instant triple talaq invalid?
x: Shayara Bano (2017) invalidated instant triple talaq; Shah Bano concerned maintenance under Section 125 CrPC.

s: By which year did Amit Shah say the Uniform Civil Code would be in place in all 21 NDA-ruled States?
x: The Home Minister set 2029 as the target for UCC in all 21 NDA-ruled States.

s: Which case cited Goa as an example of a common civil code?
x: Jose Paulo Coutinho (2019) cited Goa; John Vallamattom struck down Section 118 of the Indian Succession Act.

s: Which statement on State-level Uniform Civil Code measures is correct?
o: Uttarakhand UCC in force since January 2025; Gujarat became the second State to get Presidential assent
Uttarakhand UCC in force since January 2024; Gujarat became the second State to get Presidential assent
Uttarakhand UCC in force since January 2025; Assam became the second State to get Presidential assent
Gujarat UCC in force since January 2025; Uttarakhand became the second State to get Presidential assent
x: Uttarakhand was the first State, with its UCC in force since January 2025; Gujarat's UCC Bill-2026 became the second to receive Presidential assent (President Droupadi Murmu).

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that conversion to another religion for a second marriage is invalid?
x: In Sarla Mudgal (1995) the Supreme Court held that converting to another religion to contract a second marriage is invalid.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court strike down Section 118 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925?
x: In John Vallamattom (2003) the Supreme Court struck down Section 118 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925.

s: The Shah Bano case (1985) dealt with maintenance under which provision?
o: Section 118 of the Indian Succession Act
Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act
x: Shah Bano (1985) was on maintenance to a divorced Muslim woman under Section 125 of the CrPC.

s: What is the principal legal effect of the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026?
o: They permit organisations to use separate regional time zones for official purposes
They make UTC+5:30 the only permissible time displayed in India
They require every organisation to own an atomic clock
They make Indian Standard Time the single legal reference for legal, administrative, commercial and official purposes
x: The Rules make Indian Standard Time the single legal reference for legal, administrative, commercial and official purposes. The tempting option that requires every organisation to own an atomic clock is wrong; organisations only need to synchronise with time traceable to IST.

s: Which Article empowers Parliament to restrict the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces?
x: Article 33 lets Parliament restrict Fundamental Rights of members of the forces. The Assam Rifles is administratively under MHA and operationally under the Army.

s: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026, which authority is required to issue a special order when registration is delayed by more than two years?
x: A special order of a First-Class Magistrate is required when registration is delayed by more than two years. For a delay of one to two years, permission from a Judicial Magistrate along with a fee is required.

s: The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Act 2026 provides a common framework for which officers?
x: The Act, in force from 8 October 2026, covers Group-A General Duty officers, not Group-B.

s: The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 come into force how many days after Gazette publication?
x: The Rules come into force 180 days after publication in the Gazette.

s: Which of the following pairs (force – year of establishment) is correctly matched?
x: CRPF was established in 1939. BSF dates to 1965 and CISF to 1969.

s: Under the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026, which body provides technical guidance?
x: CSIR-NPL provides technical guidance while the Legal Metrology Department enforces the Rules; other time zones may be shown only along with IST.

s: Which organisation became the 46th terrorist organisation in the First Schedule of the UAPA, 1967 on September 16, 2026?
x: The MHA declared the Pakistan-based Shehzad Bhatti Network a terrorist organisation under the UAPA, making it the 46th in the First Schedule.

s: NavIC (earlier IRNSS), developed after GPS data was denied during the Kargil War, carries which type of clocks?
x: NavIC, earlier IRNSS, was developed after GPS data was denied during the Kargil War and carries atomic clocks.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Shehzad Bhatti Network and Section 35 of the UAPA?
o: The network was involved in cross-border smuggling of arms, explosives and narcotics.
Section 35 enables only removal, and not addition, of organisations.
Section 35 enables the Centre to remove organisations from the First Schedule.
Section 35 enables the Centre to add organisations to the First Schedule.
x: Section 35 empowers the Centre both to add and to remove organisations in the First Schedule.

s: On which date did the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026 receive Presidential assent?
x: Assent came on 6 August 2026; the Act extends anthem-level protection to Vande Mataram.

s: Which one of the following is an incorrect statement regarding the seven pillars of PRAHAAR?
o: Prevention is one of the pillars
Human Rights is one of the pillars
Recovery and Resilience is one of the pillars
Border Management is one of the pillars
x: Border Management is not listed among PRAHAAR's seven pillars. The listed pillars include Prevention, Human Rights, and Recovery and Resilience.

s: On which date did the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 come into force?
x: The Act came into force on October 1, 2026; it had received Presidential assent in August 2026.

s: On which date did Amit Shah unveil PRAHAAR, India's counter-terrorism policy?
x: Amit Shah unveiled PRAHAAR, a 10-year framework, on 23 February 2026. 28 September 2026 was the date of the PRAHAAR conference in New Delhi.

s: Which Central Armed Police Force, established in 1962, is associated with the China border?
x: The ITBP was established in 1962 and is associated with the China border. BSF, CISF and SSB are linked respectively with Pakistan and Bangladesh borders, infrastructure and airports, and Nepal and Bhutan borders.

s: Which time-dissemination technology offers microsecond accuracy?
x: PTP gives microseconds; NTP gives milliseconds, satellite links nanoseconds and optical links picoseconds.

s: Indian Standard Time, maintained by CSIR-NPL, has an uncertainty versus UTC of less than how much?
x: IST (UTC+5:30) is kept within 3 nanoseconds of UTC by CSIR-NPL, India's National Metrology Institute.

s: In which year was the original Registration of Births and Deaths Act enacted?
x: The RBD Act dates from 1969; its 2026 amendment came into force on 1 October 2026.

s: Where was the White Rabbit-based IST network commissioned in July 2026?
x: It was commissioned at the Regional Reference Standard Laboratory, Bengaluru, one of 5 RRSLs.

s: What is the name of India's first National Counter-Terrorism Policy and Strategy, unveiled in February 2026?
x: PRAHAAR (Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism) is India's first national counter-terrorism policy, unveiled by Amit Shah on 23 February 2026.

s: Who has operational control of the Assam Rifles?
x: The Assam Rifles is under the administrative control of the MHA but the operational control of the Army.

s: What is the full form of PRAHAAR, India's first national counter-terrorism policy?
o: Policy for Rapid Action Against Hostile Agents and Radicals
Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism
Programme for Rapid Action Against Hostile Armed Radicals
Plan for Response and Action Against Hostile Attacks and Raids
x: PRAHAAR stands for Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism, unveiled on 23 February 2026.

s: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026 extended anthem-level protection to which of the following?
x: The 2026 amendment extends anthem-level protection to Vande Mataram; obstructing it can draw up to 3 years in jail.

s: Who is the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, the authority under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act?
x: Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan is the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, the authority under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act; the nodal ministry is MHA.

s: Which Central Armed Police Force guards the Nepal and Bhutan borders?
x: The SSB (1963) guards the Nepal and Bhutan borders.

s:
Assertion (A): World Mental Health Day is observed every year on 10 October.
Reason (R): World Mental Health Day was first observed in 1992.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true: the day falls on 10 October and was first observed in 1992, but the year of its first observance does not explain the date chosen.

s: Vande Mataram, which was at the centre of the 2026 Supreme Court proceedings, was written by whom and first sung by whom at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress?
x: Vande Mataram was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and was first sung by Tagore at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress. T.M. Krishna was the musician who challenged the direction concerning the song, not its author or first singer.

s: Which of the following about the Supreme Court's power under Article 142 is NOT correct?
o: It is a power of the Supreme Court.
It is unlimited and can override fundamental constitutional limits.
It cannot override fundamental constitutional limits.
x: Article 142 is broad but not unlimited; it cannot override fundamental constitutional limits, so the claim that it is unlimited is false.

s: Who was appointed Chair of the Standing Committee on Judicial Well-Being constituted by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant?
x: Justice K.V. Viswanathan was appointed Chair of the Standing Committee on Judicial Well-Being, constituted on 10 October 2026 by CJI Surya Kant. Dr Savita Malhotra, Rajat Mitra and Mrinal Kanwar were listed as members, not Chair.

s: The Judicial Well-Being Committee constituted by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant was based on research by which institution?
o: Centre for Research and Planning of the Supreme Court
x: The committee was based on research by the Supreme Court's Centre for Research and Planning. PGIMER was associated with Dr Savita Malhotra's membership, while the World Federation for Mental Health is associated with the origin of World Mental Health Day.

s: Under Article 22(1), how must the grounds of arrest be communicated to the accused?
o: in writing, only in PMLA and UAPA cases
in writing and in a language the accused understands
x: Grounds of arrest must be given in writing in a language the accused understands for all offences, including PMLA and UAPA.

s: Which service did the Supreme Court launch on Hindi Diwas, September 14, 2026, to make its judgments easier to understand?
x: The Supreme Court launched Jan Suchna Seva, offering simplified judgments and 15–30 minute audio-visual explainers.

s: Under the ruling on written grounds of arrest, whose permission is needed to re-arrest a person?
x: Re-arrest requires written grounds and the permission of a Judicial Magistrate; the probe must also go to another officer.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. High Courts also possess the power under Article 142 to do complete justice.
2. Article 142(2) deals with constitutional remedies and is called the heart and soul of the Constitution.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Both are wrong: Article 142 power belongs only to the Supreme Court, and Article 142(2) concerns attendance, documents and contempt; 'heart and soul' refers to Article 32.

s: For remand, written grounds of arrest must be supplied at least how long before production?
x: The ruling requires written grounds at least 2 hours before production for remand, else the arrest is illegal; Section 47 BNSS also covers grounds and bail rights.

s: Why did the Supreme Court invoke Article 142 in the NEET-UG paper-leak matter?
o: To quash FIRs against protesting students
To transfer the matter to a High Court
To impose disciplinary action on students
x: The Supreme Court used Article 142, the power to do complete justice, to quash FIRs against students protesting the NEET-UG paper leak. The ruling was not a transfer of the matter or a review of examination results.

s: Who challenged the Ministry of Home Affairs direction of February 2026 requiring the singing of all six stanzas of Vande Mataram before the Supreme Court?
x: Carnatic musician T.M. Krishna challenged the February 2026 direction concerning all six stanzas of Vande Mataram. CJI Surya Kant and Justice V. Mohan were members of the bench, not the person who brought the challenge.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court proceedings on singing all stanzas of Vande Mataram?
o: The Bijoe Emmanuel principles involved Articles 19(1)(a) and 25.
The bench included CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi.
The Court observed that criminal action should not be initiated against a person declining on genuine religious grounds.
The Centre was directed to reply in three weeks.
x: The Centre was directed to reply in two weeks, not three weeks.

s: Khairatabad MLA Danam Nagender was disqualified by the Telangana High Court under which provision of the Tenth Schedule?
x: He was disqualified under Paragraph 2(1)(a) of the Tenth Schedule, with effect from April 23, 2024.

s: Under Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule, who decides disqualification on grounds of defection?
x: Paragraph 6 gives the decision to the Speaker, subject to judicial review; Article 192 (Governor) concerns other disqualifications.

s: Which Article did Dr B.R. Ambedkar call the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
x: Article 32 (constitutional remedies) is the 'heart and soul'; Article 142 is the Supreme Court's complete-justice power.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment added the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection) to the Constitution?
x: The Tenth Schedule came with the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

s: The Supreme Court is examining the Vande Mataram stanzas challenge under the principles of which case?
x: The bench of CJI Surya Kant will apply Bijoe Emmanuel (1986) principles under Articles 19(1)(a) and 25.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court ruling on grounds of arrest?
o: Grounds must be in a language the accused understands
It applies to all offences, including PMLA and UAPA
Re-arrest needs permission of a Judicial Magistrate
It excludes offences under the UAPA
x: The ruling covers all offences, including PMLA and UAPA, so the exclusion is wrong.

s: Which Section of the BNSS requires that an arrested person be informed of the grounds of arrest and of the right to bail?
x: Section 47 of the BNSS requires the police to tell an arrested person the grounds of arrest and the right to bail.

s: Under which Article can the President seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court?
x: Article 143 provides for the President's advisory reference to the Supreme Court.

s: Whose decision on the defection petition against Khairatabad MLA Danam Nagender did the Telangana High Court set aside in September 2026?
x: The Telangana HC bench of CJ Aparesh Kumar Singh and Justice G.M. Mohiuddin set aside Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar's decision and disqualified Danam Nagender.

s: Under Article 192, who decides questions of disqualification of a State legislator other than those under the Tenth Schedule?
x: Under Article 192 the Governor decides other disqualifications (acting on the opinion of the Election Commission); Tenth Schedule cases go to the Speaker.

s: On which date was the Supreme Court of India inaugurated?
x: The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950, two days after the Constitution came into force.

s: Under the Inter-State Council (Amendment) Order, 2026, who attends the Inter-State Council when Article 356 is in force?
x: The Governor attends the Inter-State Council when Article 356 is in force. The Lieutenant Governor of Delhi attends when Article 239AB applies.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Article 371F relates to Sikkim. Article 371A is for Nagaland, 371D for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and 371J for Karnataka.

s: After Uttarakhand, which State became the second to receive approval for its Uniform Civil Code Bill–2026?
x: Gujarat became the second State after President Droupadi Murmu assented to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill–2026. Uttarakhand was the first State to implement the Uniform Civil Code, making it the closest trap.

s: What was proposed for the Union Territory of Ladakh in the MHA meeting held in New Delhi on September 9, 2026?
o: A directly elected governing body under Article 371J with safeguards only for language
Statehood with inclusion under the Sixth Schedule
A nominated governing body under Article 371 with safeguards only for forests
A directly elected governing body with safeguards for land, culture and language, linked to Article 240
x: The MHA proposal envisaged a directly elected governing body for Ladakh, along with safeguards on land, culture and language, linked to Article 240. Statehood and Sixth Schedule status were sought by the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, but were not the MHA proposal described here.

s: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution applies to tribal areas in which of the following States?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
x: The Sixth Schedule, linked with Articles 244(2) and 275(1), applies to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Central Zonal Council?
x: The Central Zonal Council is headquartered at Allahabad; Northern, Eastern and Western are at New Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai.

s: What is the headquarters of the North Eastern Council?
x: The North Eastern Council has its headquarters at Shillong. Chennai, New Delhi and Allahabad are headquarters associated with other councils.

s: Which body organises the meetings of the Zonal Councils?
x: The Inter-State Council Secretariat organises Zonal Council meetings.

s: Who chairs the Zonal Councils set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
x: The Union Home Minister chairs the Zonal Councils; Chief Ministers serve as Vice-Chairmen by rotation.

s: Who chairs the Inter-State Council, set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice?
x: The Inter-State Council is chaired by the Prime Minister.

s: Under the Bihar–Jharkhand Son river water agreement, what is Bihar's share?
x: Bihar's share is 5.75 MAF; Jharkhand's is 2.0 MAF, making a total of 7.75 MAF.

s: In September 2026, Karnataka made which language the second additional administrative language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi?
x: Tulu was made the second additional administrative language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi; it is not in the Eighth Schedule.

s: The proposed special constitutional arrangement for Ladakh discussed in September 2026 was titled what?
x: The proposal was titled “Chapter K” under Article 371. The alternatives change the chapter designation and therefore do not identify the proposal.

s: Where does the Son river rise?
x: The Son rises on the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh and joins the Ganga west of Patna.

s: The decision concerning Tulu as an additional administrative language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi was based on whose committee report?
x: The decision was based on the committee of educationist M. Mohan Alva, whose report was submitted in 2023. The other names are associated with different political or administrative contexts in the listed developments.

s: For which region was Article 371-K proposed?
x: Article 371-K was proposed for Ladakh in September 2026.

s: Article 371D contains special provisions for which State(s)?
x: Article 371D is for AP and Telangana; Ladakh's proposal is Article 371-K, Karnataka is 371J and Sikkim 371F.

s: Where was the 28th Western Zonal Council meeting held on 7 September 2026?
x: Amit Shah chaired it at Panaji, Goa; Mumbai is the Western Council's headquarters.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Tulu?
o: It is listed in the Eighth Schedule
It is an additional administrative language in Udupi
Its use followed M. Mohan Alva's committee report
x: Tulu is not in the Eighth Schedule; the other statements are correct.

s: Who chairs the JPC examining the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 on One Nation One Election?
x: The Joint Parliamentary Committee on the ONOE Bill is chaired by P.P. Chaudhary.

s: One Nation One Election is proposed through which Constitution Amendment Bill?
x: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 provides for simultaneous elections.

s: Who won the Nagaon (Assam) Lok Sabha by-election counted on 9 October 2026?
x: BJP's Debasish Sharma beat AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal; the seat fell vacant when Pradyut Bordoloi won Dispur.

s: Which party won both Tamil Nadu Assembly by-elections (Madurantakam and Dharapuram) in October 2026?
x: The ruling TVK won both Madurantakam and Dharapuram.

s: The Thattanchavady (Puducherry) Assembly seat fell vacant on the resignation of whom?
x: It fell vacant when CM N. Rangasamy resigned; AINRC's Ashok Anand won the by-election.

s:
Consider the following statements about the by-elections of October 2026:
1. The BJP won both West Bengal Assembly seats.
2. Nagaon in Assam is an Assembly seat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct: the BJP won Nandigram and Rejinagar. Nagaon is a Lok Sabha seat.

s: On which date did the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, renaming Kerala as Keralam, come into force?
x: It came into force on 25 August 2026 by MHA notification; Rajya Sabha passed it on 12 August.

s: On 2 October 2026, MHA standardised the names of how many places and features in Ladakh?
x: 28 places and geographical features in Ladakh were given standard names on the Survey of India map.

s: Which country called the standardisation of place names in Ladakh 'illegal and void'?
x: China called it illegal and void; the MEA rejected the claim.

s: Which order did President Droupadi Murmu amend under Article 263 in September 2026?
x: The Inter-State Council (Amendment) Order 2026, notified on 9 September 2026, amended the Inter-State Council Order, 1990 under Article 263.

s: Since which date has Ladakh been a Union Territory?
x: Ladakh became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019.

s: Article 371, under which special provisions for several States (and the proposed Article 371-K for Ladakh) fall, is in which Part of the Constitution?
x: Article 371 and its sub-articles are in Part XXI (Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions).

s: Under which Article of the Constitution was Kerala renamed Keralam by an Act of Parliament in 2026?
x: Article 3 lets Parliament alter the name, area or boundaries of a State after the President refers the Bill to the State legislature for its views.

s:
Match the following Zonal Councils with their headquarters:
List-I
A. Northern
B. Eastern
C. Southern
D. Western
List-II
1. Chennai
2. Mumbai
3. New Delhi
4. Kolkata
x: Northern - New Delhi, Eastern - Kolkata, Southern - Chennai, Western - Mumbai.

s: Undivided Bihar's 7.75 MAF share of Son river water, now divided between Bihar and Jharkhand, comes from which agreement?
x: The 7.75 MAF was undivided Bihar's share under the 1973 Bansagar Agreement among MP, UP and undivided Bihar.

s: Betting and gambling fall under which entry of the Seventh Schedule?
x: State List Entry 34 covers betting and gambling; Union List Entry 40 covers lotteries organised by governments.

s: Which Section of the Lotteries (Regulation) Act, 1998 permits a State to ban lotteries organised by other States?
x: Section 5 permits a State to ban other States' lotteries; Section 6 concerns the Union's power.

s: Which case treated lotteries as actionable claims and goods under GST?
x: Skill Lotto Solutions held lotteries to be actionable claims and goods under GST; B.R. Enterprises is linked to the all-or-nothing rule.

s: Under Section 115BB, at what rate are winnings from lotteries taxed?
x: Winnings are taxed at 30% under Section 115BB; 40% is the GST rate on lotteries.

s: From 22 September 2025, what is the rate of GST on lotteries, betting, casinos and online money gaming?
x: These attract 40% GST from 22 September 2025.

s: According to a Lok Sabha reply of March 2023, how many States run lotteries?
x: Nine States run lotteries, including Kerala, Goa, Punjab, Sikkim and West Bengal.

s: Which case laid down the 'all-or-nothing' rule on lotteries?
x: B.R. Enterprises (1999) gave the all-or-nothing rule, after which Tamil Nadu and Karnataka went lottery-free.

s: Under which entry of the Seventh Schedule do lotteries organised by the Union or State governments fall?
x: Union List Entry 40 covers government lotteries; betting and gambling are State List Entry 34.

s: With reference to the taxation framework for lotteries, betting, casinos and online money gaming, which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: GST is levied at 40% from September 22, 2025.
Winnings are taxed at 20% under Section 115BB.
Tax deducted at source on winnings is covered by Section 194B.
Winnings are taxed at 30% under Section 115BB.
x: The incorrect statement is that winnings are taxed at 20% under Section 115BB; the applicable rate stated is 30%. The same framework provides for 40% GST from September 22, 2025, and TDS under Section 194B.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that gambling is res extra commercium?
x: R.M.D. Chamarbaugwala (1957) held gambling to be res extra commercium (not a protected trade).

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
s:
Consider the following statements regarding Om Prakash Mathur:

1. He is the current Governor of Sikkim. (As of March 2025)

2. He was previously a member of Rajya Sabha from Rajasthan.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Which State's Assembly introduced India's first comprehensive Elderly Care Bill in October 2026?
x: Kerala became the first State with a dedicated comprehensive bill for elderly welfare when its Assembly introduced the Elderly Care Bill on 16 October 2026.

s: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, who is a senior citizen?
x: The 2007 Act defines a senior citizen as a person aged 60 or above. The International Day of Older Persons is 1 October.

s: In October 2026, the Union Government capped MRP-based trade margins for non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines at what level?
x: The Union Government approved a 30% cap on MRP-based trade margins for non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA)?
o: It has its headquarters in Mumbai.
It works under the Department of Pharmaceuticals.
It regulates prices under the DPCO 2013.
x: NPPA has its headquarters in New Delhi, not Mumbai; the other statements are correct.

s: The CAFE-III norms aim at what improvement in car fuel efficiency by 2032?
x: CAFE-III targets a 16.7% improvement in car fuel efficiency by 2032.

s: Under the CAFE-III norms, what incentive multiplier do strong hybrids get?
x: Strong hybrids get 1.6x; BEVs and REEVs get 3x and PHEVs 2.5x.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CAFE-III norms will be in force from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032.
2. Under the CAFE-III norms, the reference mass is raised from 1,082 kg to 1,329 kg.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. The reference mass is raised from 1,082 kg to 1,229 kg, not 1,329 kg.

s: The draft FSSAI infant nutrition amendment (2026) proposes prohibiting sucrose and fructose in foods for infants under what age?
x: The draft, gazetted on 16 October 2026, covers foods for infants under six months; FSSAI is under the Health Ministry.

s: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) functions under which Act?
x: FSSAI functions under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and has its headquarters in New Delhi.

s: What is the qualifying date for the Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 States and UTs announced in October 2026?
x: The ECI's Special Summary Revision in 17 States and UTs uses 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18?
x: The 61st Amendment, 1988 lowered the voting age to 18. Article 324 gives the ECI control over electoral rolls.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Section 21(2) – Representation of the People Act, 1950
x: The 61st Amendment that lowered the voting age to 18 was made in 1988, not 1989.

s: Where was the National Conference on E-Governance Reforms-2026 held in October 2026?
x: DARPG and the Himachal Pradesh government organised the conference in Dharamshala on 16-17 October 2026.

s: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) is under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
x: DARPG is under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions. Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.

s: In which year was the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) approved?
x: NeGP was approved in 2006; Digital India came in 2015 and Himachal Pradesh became a State in 1971.

s: Which became India's first ISO-certified disaster response force in October 2026?
o: Himachal Pradesh State Disaster Response Force
x: The Uttarakhand SDRF became India's first ISO-certified disaster response force with an ISO Quality Management System certification.

s: In which year was the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) established?
x: The NDRF was established in 2006 under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.

s: In October 2026, Telangana's mandal-level El Niño coordination committees were to be chaired by whom?
x: The committees are chaired by MPDOs and report to the District Collectors, who were directed to form them.

s: El Niño, the warm phase of ENSO, involves above-normal sea surface temperatures in which region?
x: El Niño brings above-normal SST in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific and is often linked to a weaker southwest monsoon.

s: Whom did the Supreme Court appoint as sole arbitrator in the KG Basin gas dispute between the Centre and Reliance Industries in 2026?
x: The Supreme Court appointed Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai as sole arbitrator, assisted by two party-nominated experts.

s: In the KG-D6 block, Reliance holds what share?
x: Reliance holds 60%, BP 30% and Niko 10%. The 2016 demand notice was for $1.47 billion.

s: In which year was the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, relevant to the KG Basin gas dispute, enacted?
x: The Act is of 1996; 1956 is when ONGC was established.

s: A Telangana ordinance of October 2026 raised the retirement age of district judicial officers from 61 to what?
x: The ordinance of 31 October 2026 raises the retirement age from 61 to 62, retrospective from 31 March 2026.

s: Under which Article did the Governor promulgate the 2026 Telangana ordinance raising judicial officers' retirement age?
x: Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla promulgated it under Article 213(1), retrospective from 31 March 2026; Article 123 is the President's power.

s: Under Article 124, at what age do Supreme Court judges retire?
x: Supreme Court judges retire at 65; High Court judges retire at 62 under Article 217.

s: How many members does the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament have?
x: The PAC has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament?
o: It was first set up in 1921.
It has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
Its members have a two-year term.
Its Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker.
x: PAC members have a one-year term, not two years; the other statements are correct.

s: Where was the Conference of PAC Chairpersons inaugurated in November 2026?
x: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla inaugurated it in Thiruvananthapuram. Union Ministers cannot be PAC members.

s: On 3 November 2026, the Supreme Court allowed only green crackers approved by which body in Delhi-NCR for 7-8 November?
x: The Supreme Court permitted only CSIR-NEERI-approved green crackers on 7-8 November 2026.

s: In Delhi-NCR, green crackers are banned within what distance of hospitals and silence zones?
x: The ban applies within 300 m of hospitals, nursing homes, old-age homes and silence zones; barium-based crackers are prohibited.

s: Where is the headquarters of CSIR-NEERI?
x: CSIR-NEERI was established in 1958 and has its headquarters in Nagpur.

s: Which became the first State with a dedicated Silt Management Policy in November 2026?
x: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary announced it on 3 November 2026 as the first dedicated State Silt Management Policy.

s: On which date was Bihar's Silt Management Policy-2026, the first such State policy, approved?
x: It was approved on 15 September and announced by CM Samrat Choudhary on 3 November 2026. The Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

s: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam-2026 replaces which rules?
x: The Niyam-2026 replaces the nearly 90-year-old Aircraft Rules, 1937.

s: Under which law is the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam-2026 framed?
x: It is framed under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 and comes into force on 1 January 2027.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about civil aviation law and bodies in India?
o: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934.
The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 came into force on 1 January 2025.
x: The DGCA is the regulator, while BCAS handles aviation security; the other statements are correct.

s: Which Ministry announced the Corporate Average Fuel Economy-III (CAFE-III) norms in October 2026?
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
x: The CAFE-III norms, aiming at a 16.7% improvement in car fuel efficiency by 2032, were announced by the Ministry of Power.

s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to make provision for public assistance in old age?
x: Article 41 (DPSP) provides for public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO)?
x: ISO was set up in 1947 and has its headquarters in Geneva.

s: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
x: The Kosi is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its floods.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
x: ICAO was set up in 1944 and has its headquarters in Montreal.

s: Who is the Union Civil Aviation Minister under whom the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam-2026 was notified?
x: Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu is the Union Civil Aviation Minister; the Civil Aviation Ministry notified the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam-2026.

s: When was the Digital India programme launched?
x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.

s: The Public Accounts Committee examines the reports of the CAG. Under which Article is the office of the CAG created?
x: The office of the CAG is created by Article 148. The PAC examines the CAG's reports.

s: What is the summer capital of Uttarakhand?
x: Uttarakhand's winter capital is Dehradun and its summer capital is Gairsain.

s: Within how many minutes does the Election Commission aim to act on a complaint made through the cVIGIL app?
x: The ECI aims to act on cVIGIL complaints of Model Code violations within 100 minutes.

s: In which year was the Public Accounts Committee first set up in India?
x: The PAC was first set up in 1921 after the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.

s: Who appoints the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament?
x: The PAC Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker, traditionally from the opposition.

s: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced which law?
x: The Adhiniyam, 2024 replaced the Aircraft Act, 1934 and came into force on 1 January 2025.

s: Under Article 217, at what age do High Court judges retire?
x: High Court judges retire at 62 (Article 217); Supreme Court judges at 65 (Article 124).

s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act of which year?
x: It amends the 1956 Act and raises the strength to 38, the first increase since 2019.

s: In 1950, what was the strength of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice of India?
x: The Supreme Court had 8 judges including the CJI in 1950, raised to 11 in 1956.

s: The 2026 Presidential Ordinance under Article 123 raised the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to how many?
x: The Ordinance raised the strength from 34 to 38 judges; five judges were then sworn in.

s: Which of the following about the Ordinance raising the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court is NOT correct?
o: It raised the strength from 34 to 38, including the CJI.
If it lapses, the strength remains at 38.
Reversion raises concerns about security of tenure and judicial independence.
If it lapses, the strength reverts to 34.
x: If the Ordinance lapses, the strength reverts to 34, not stays at 38.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment, 2026?
o: Article 124(1) lets Parliament fix the number of judges by law
It raised puisne judges from 33 to 36
Total strength including the CJI became 38
It amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956
x: Puisne judges were raised from 33 to 37, not 36; total strength including the CJI is 38.

s: As what kind of Bill was the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, which replaced a May 2026 ordinance, passed?
x: It was passed as a Money Bill; the Rajya Sabha only returned it and did not reject it.

s: The India Justice Report 2025 placed the number of judges in India at about how many per million population?
x: The India Justice Report 2025 put it at about 15.9 judges per million; 50 per million is the Law Commission's recommendation.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1986) – Repeated re-promulgation of Ordinances is unconstitutional
SC Advocates-on-Record Association (2015) – 99th Amendment and NJAC Act struck down
Article 13(3)(a) – “Law” includes custom or usage having the force of law
Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (2017) – 99th Amendment and NJAC Act struck down
x: Krishna Kumar Singh held that an Ordinance is not a substitute for legislation; the NJAC was struck down in the Advocates-on-Record Association case.

s: An ordinance ceases to operate, unless approved, after how long from the reassembly of Parliament?
x: An ordinance lapses six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved.

s: Which case held that repeated re-promulgation of ordinances is unconstitutional?
o: Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (2017)
D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1986)
Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala (1986)
x: D.C. Wadhwa (1986) struck at repeated re-promulgation; Krishna Kumar Singh (2017) held an ordinance is not a substitute for legislation.

s: Along with the NJAC Act, which Constitutional Amendment did the SC Advocates-on-Record Association case (2015) strike down?
x: The 2015 judgment struck down the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act.

s: The Law Commission recommended how many judges per million population?
x: The Law Commission recommended 50 judges per million, against about 15.9 per the India Justice Report 2025.

s: About how many cases were pending in the Supreme Court on 1 January 2026?
x: SC pendency was about 92,101; in 2025, 75,410 cases were filed and 65,615 disposed of.

s: Under Article 13(3)(a) of the Constitution, which of the following is included in the definition of 'law'?
o: Custom or usage having the force of law
x: Article 13(3)(a) says 'law' includes any ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, and custom or usage having the force of law.

s: What is a 'puisne judge' of the Supreme Court?
o: A retired judge asked to sit under Article 128
A judge of the Supreme Court other than the Chief Justice of India
An ad hoc judge appointed under Article 127
An acting Chief Justice under Article 126
x: A puisne judge is any Supreme Court judge other than the CJI; the 2026 Ordinance raised their number from 33 to 37.

s: Which Article allows the CJI, with the President's consent, to request a retired Supreme Court judge to sit and act as a judge?
x: Article 128 covers retired judges sitting in the Supreme Court; Article 127 is for ad hoc judges.

s: Which Article of the Constitution gives the Supreme Court the power to review its own judgments?
x: Article 137 gives the Supreme Court power to review its judgments or orders.

s: What was the strength of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice of India, after the increase of 1956?
x: The strength (including the CJI) was 8 in 1950 and was raised to 11 in 1956; it reached 34 in 2019 and 38 in 2026.

s: Before the 2026 increase to 38, in which year was the strength of the Supreme Court last raised (from 31 to 34)?
x: The 2026 increase was the first since 2019, when the strength was raised from 31 to 34.

s: What is the minimum number of judges required to form a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court?
x: A Constitution Bench has at least 5 judges.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that an ordinance is not a substitute for legislation?
o: D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1986)
Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (2017)
A.K. Roy v. Union of India (1982)
x: Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (2017) held that an ordinance is not a substitute for legislation; D.C. Wadhwa (1986) was on re-promulgation.

s: Which Article of the Constitution makes every High Court a court of record?
x: Article 215 makes High Courts courts of record; Article 129 does so for the Supreme Court.

s: Which Article of the Constitution allows Parliament to fix the number of Supreme Court judges by law?
x: Article 124(1) lets Parliament prescribe the number of SC judges by law, so no constitutional amendment is needed.

s: Under Section 187(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, what is the maximum total period of police custody that may be sought in parts during the initial period?
x: Police custody may be sought in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days, but the total police custody is capped at 15 days. The periods of 40 and 60 days relate to the window for seeking custody, not the maximum custody itself.

s: In the Supreme Court verdict refining the legal definition of ‘industry’, which description is correct?
o: A 9-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI Surya Kant, delivering a 6:3 majority verdict
A 7-judge Bench led by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer, delivering a 6:3 majority verdict
A 9-judge Constitution Bench led by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer, delivering a 7:3 majority verdict
A 7-judge Bench led by CJI Surya Kant, delivering a 9:6 majority verdict
x: The verdict was delivered by a 9-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI Surya Kant by a 6:3 majority. The 7-judge Bench led by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer was associated with the earlier Bangalore Water Supply case and its Triple Test.

s: Under the BNSS, beyond how long may no person be detained without being produced before a magistrate?
x: Detention beyond 24 hours without production before a magistrate is barred; total police custody is capped at 15 days.

s: Under Section 187(3) of the BNSS, detention in cases punishable with death, life or 10+ years may extend up to how many days before default bail?
x: Detention may extend to 90 days in such cases and 60 days in others, after which default bail follows.

s: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 merged the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 and which other Act?
x: The Code merged the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 with the two other Acts; the Supreme Court held the 1947 definition of ‘industry’ cannot apply unchanged.

s: Which Article provides for equal justice and free legal aid as a Directive Principle of State Policy?
x: Article 39A provides for equal justice and free legal aid.

s: Which Article gives an arrested person the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice?
x: Article 22(1) guarantees counsel of choice; Article 21 includes a fair trial within the right to life.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rulings on Bar Associations and representation of accused persons?
o: Kuldeep Agarwal (2019) held that refusal in special circumstances is a matter for the Bar Association
A.S. Mohammed Rafi v. State of Tamil Nadu was decided by the Supreme Court in 2010
A.S. Mohammed Rafi held boycott resolutions wholly illegal, null and void
x: Kuldeep Agarwal held that refusal in special circumstances is for an individual advocate, not the Bar.

s:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court held that the right to walk on footpaths is a fundamental right under Articles 20 and 21.
Reason (R): Pedestrians take precedence over vehicles on footpaths.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is false because the Supreme Court located the right under Articles 19(1)(d) and 21, not Article 20 and Article 21. Reason R is true: pedestrians take precedence over vehicles.

s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the definition of 'industry'?
o: The issue was decided by the Election Commission under Article 324.
The 1978 Bangalore Water Supply definition automatically applies to the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
A nine-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant held in August 2026 that the 1978 definition does not apply to the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
A five-judge Bench held in November 2025 that the Industrial Relations Code is unconstitutional.
x: In August 2026, a nine-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant held that the 1978 Bangalore Water Supply definition does not apply to the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.

s: Which Supreme Court case held that the creamy layer principle does not apply to SCs and STs?
x: Ashoka Kumar Thakur (2008) held the creamy layer does not apply to SCs and STs; Indra Sawhney upheld it for OBCs.

s: What did the seven-judge bench hold in Davinder Singh (August 2024) regarding SC/ST reservations?
o: The creamy layer automatically applies to SCs and STs
States may undertake sub-categorisation of SCs and STs
Only Parliament may notify the SC and ST lists
The creamy layer applies to OBCs and SCs alike
x: In Davinder Singh, the seven-judge bench allowed States to undertake sub-categorisation of SCs and STs. The other options concern different constitutional or reservation issues and do not state the holding identified in this case.

s: Which position was associated with the Centre in August 2026 regarding reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: It transferred the issue entirely to local bodies.
It supported a creamy layer within SC/ST reservations.
It proposed abolition of SC/ST reservations.
It opposed a creamy layer within SC/ST reservations.
x: In August 2026, the Centre was noted as opposing the introduction of a creamy layer for SCs and STs.

s: Which High Court held in 2025 that a Bar Association is not a trade union?
x: The Madras High Court (2025) said so; the Karnataka High Court (2020) said obstructing lawyers for Kashmiri students may be contempt.

s: To which group does the creamy layer principle in reservations currently apply?
x: The creamy layer currently applies to OBCs; the Centre opposed petitions seeking to extend it to SC/ST reservations.

s: Under Articles 341 and 342, who notifies the lists of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
x: The President notifies the SC/ST lists under Articles 341 and 342. Changes to these lists can be made only by an Act of Parliament, which makes Parliament the tempting but incorrect option.

s: In which case was the 'Triple Test' for defining 'industry' laid down?
o: Bangalore Water Supply v. A. Rajappa (1978)
x: The 7-judge bench of Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer laid down the Triple Test in Bangalore Water Supply (1978).

s: Which case held that any creamy-layer exclusion among Scheduled Castes must come from Parliament?
x: E.V. Chinnaiah (2005) held so; Ashoka Kumar Thakur said the creamy layer does not apply to SC/STs.

s: Under Section 38 of the BNSS, when may an accused meet an advocate of his choice?
o: During interrogation, though not throughout it
Only after the charge-sheet is filed
x: Section 38 BNSS allows the accused to meet an advocate during interrogation, but not throughout the interrogation.

s: From which State did the case State vs Suda Suresh Veera Venkata Naga Raju, in which the Supreme Court explained police custody under Section 187(2) BNSS, arise?
x: State of Andhra Pradesh vs Suda Suresh Veera Venkata Naga Raju arose from a custodial death probe in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which Supreme Court case upheld OBC reservation and introduced the creamy layer for OBCs?
x: Indra Sawhney (1992) upheld the OBC quota and brought in the creamy layer for OBCs.

s: Who headed the seven-judge bench that laid down the 'Triple Test' for 'industry' in Bangalore Water Supply v. A. Rajappa (1978)?
x: The 1978 Bangalore Water Supply case was decided by a 7-judge bench of Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer.

s: Which Ministry implements the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023?
x: MeitY implements the DPDP Act, 2023; the Right to be Forgotten is treated as part of privacy under Article 21.

s: In which case did the Delhi High Court issue guidelines on the Right to be Forgotten?
o: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
Dharamraj Bhanushankar Dave v. State of Gujarat
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
Laksh Vir Singh Yadav v. Union of India
x: The Delhi High Court guidelines came in Laksh Vir Singh Yadav v. Union of India; Puttaswamy (2017) established privacy as a Fundamental Right.

s: The Delhi High Court order of 29 May 2026 concerning limited online discoverability of judicial records primarily dealt with which issue?
o: Election rules for Nicobar Tribal Councils
Appointment of judges to the Supreme Court
Right to be forgotten versus open justice
Validity of the National Judicial Appointments Commission Act
x: The order concerned the right to be forgotten and the limited online discoverability of judicial records, balanced against open justice. The Nicobar election rules relate to a separate governance issue, not this Delhi High Court order.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indian privacy and right-to-be-forgotten cases?
o: K.S. Puttaswamy recognised privacy as a fundamental right
In Dharamraj Bhanushankar Dave, the Gujarat High Court denied removal of acquittal details
The Orissa High Court (2020) held the right to be forgotten automatic in ongoing proceedings
x: The Orissa High Court (2020) only called for debate on the right to be forgotten in the context of online sexual abuse; it did not hold the right automatic.

s: The right to be forgotten is linked to informational privacy under which Article?
x: It flows from informational privacy under Article 21; the DPDP Act's erasure right is unclear for court records.

s: Which High Court held in 2023 that the right to be forgotten is not automatic for ongoing proceedings?
x: The Kerala High Court (2023) held so; the Supreme Court (2022) had a couple's details removed from search engines.

s: For whom mainly do Justice Sachin Datta's guidelines let search engines delist judgments?
o: Acquitted persons, private civil disputes and non-parties
x: Delisting is mainly for acquitted persons, private civil disputes and non-parties.

s: Which case held privacy to be a fundamental right, including informational privacy?
o: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
x: Puttaswamy (2017) made privacy a fundamental right; Rajagopal (1994) spoke of the right to be let alone.

s: In European law (GDPR), what is the right to be forgotten called?
x: European law calls it the right to erasure; India's DPDP Act, 2023 also recognises erasure.

s: Which Supreme Court case of 1994 recognised the 'right to be let alone'?
o: Rajagopal v. State of Tamil Nadu
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
Kharak Singh v. State of UP
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
x: Rajagopal v. State of Tamil Nadu (1994) spoke of the right to be let alone, while holding court records open to comment.

s: Under the draft Andaman and Nicobar Islands Tribal Councils Election Rules, 2026, how is the Chief Captain of each Island Tribal Council to be chosen?
x: The draft proposes a direct vote for the Chief Captain; Nicobarese leaders fear this may weaken consensus-based customary self-governance.

s: According to the Supreme Court, what should happen to a citizenship case the ECI finds doubtful during electoral-roll revision?
o: Referred to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955
Deferred until after the next election
Decided finally by the ECI itself
x: Doubtful cases go to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955, preferably before the next election in that constituency; the ECI does not finally decide citizenship.

s: Under Section 16 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which person cannot be registered as a voter?
o: A person assisted by judicial officers during a hearing
A person whose name was deleted with reasons published
A person whose identity was established through Aadhaar
x: Section 16 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, provides that a non-citizen cannot be registered as a voter. The provision relates to preparation and revision of electoral rolls.

s: In ADR v. Election Commission of India, what did the Supreme Court do with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) before the Bihar elections?
o: Transferred the SIR to the Citizenship Act authority
Suspended all roll revisions until after the elections
x: The Court upheld the ECI’s SIR order as broadly proportionate, holding the ECI best placed to decide the revision method.

s: A person's name on the electoral roll gives what kind of presumption of citizenship?
x: A name on the roll gives only an evidentiary presumption; the ECI may examine citizenship prima facie but cannot finally declare a non-citizen.
